questions.prompt: For the nuclide symbol \(^{A}_{Z}X\), state what \(A\), \(Z\), and \(N\) represent.
questions.answer:
\(Z\) is the proton number, \(N\) is the neutron number, and \(A\) is the total nucleon number. They are related by
\[
A=Z+N
\]

questions.prompt: Find the number of protons and neutrons in \(^{238}_{92}\mathrm U\).
questions.answer:
The proton number is \(Z=92\). The neutron number is
\[
N=A-Z=238-92=146
\]

questions.prompt: What is the charge of a nucleus with proton number \(Z=26\)?
questions.answer:
The nuclear charge is
\[
q=+Ze=+26e
\]
In coulombs this is \(26(1.60	imes10^{-19})=4.16	imes10^{-18}\,\mathrm C\).

questions.prompt: Define isotopes and give the condition on \(Z\) and \(N\).
questions.answer: Isotopes are nuclei of the same element with the same proton number \(Z\) but different neutron number \(N\). Therefore they have different mass number \(A\).

questions.prompt: Using \(R=R_0A^{1/3}\), find the ratio of radii for nuclei with \(A=216\) and \(A=27\).
questions.answer:
\[
 rac{R_{216}}{R_{27}}=\left( rac{216}{27}ight)^{1/3}=8^{1/3}=2
\]
The heavier nucleus has twice the radius.

questions.prompt: If \(R_0=1.2\,\mathrm{fm}\), estimate the radius of a nucleus with \(A=125\).
Show that the radius law \(R=R_0A^{1/3}\) implies nuclear volume is proportional to \(A\).
questions.answer:
The volume is
\[
V= rac43\pi R^3= rac43\pi (R_0A^{1/3})^3= rac43\pi R_0^3A
\]
Thus \(V\propto A\).

questions.prompt: Use \(R=R_0A^{1/3}\) and \(M\approx Au\) to show that nuclear density is approximately independent of \(A\).
questions.answer:
\[
ho\approx rac{Au}{(4/3)\pi R^3}= rac{Au}{(4/3)\pi R_0^3A}= rac{3u}{4\pi R_0^3}
\]
The factor \(A\) cancels, so the density is nearly constant.

questions.prompt: Estimate nuclear density using \(u=1.66\times10^{-27}\,\mathrm{kg}\) and \(R_0=1.2\times10^{-15}\,\mathrm m\).
questions.answer:
\[
ho\approx rac{3u}{4\pi R_0^3}= rac{3(1.66	imes10^{-27})}{4\pi(1.2	imes10^{-15})^3}
\]
\[
ho\approx2.3	imes10^{17}\,\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}
\]
This is many orders of magnitude above ordinary material density.

questions.prompt: A neutral atom has \(Z=17\) and \(A=35\). How many electrons, protons, and neutrons does it contain?
questions.answer:
A neutral atom has electrons equal to protons, so it has 17 electrons and 17 protons. The neutron number is
\[
N=35-17=18
\]

questions.prompt: Explain the difference between isotopes and isobars.
questions.answer: Isotopes have the same \(Z\) and different \(A\). Isobars have the same \(A\) but different \(Z\). Isotopes are the same element; isobars are generally different elements.

questions.prompt: An alpha particle is \(^{4}_{2}\mathrm{He}\). State its charge, proton number, neutron number, and nucleon number.
questions.answer:
It has \(Z=2\), \(A=4\), and
\[
N=A-Z=2
\]
Its charge is \(+2e\).

questions.prompt: A nucleus has radius \(7.2\,\mathrm{fm}\) with \(R_0=1.2\,\mathrm{fm}\). Estimate \(A\).
questions.answer: \[\nA=\left(\frac{R}{R_0}\right)^3=\left(\frac{7.2}{1.2}\right)^3=6^3=216\n\]

questions.prompt: Two nuclei have the same radius within a simple \(R=R_0A^{1/3}\) model. What can you infer about their mass numbers?
questions.answer: The radius depends only on \(A\) in this model. If the radii are the same, then the mass numbers are the same. They may still have different \(Z\) values, making them isobars.

questions.prompt: Why does the radius law support the idea that nucleons are packed with roughly constant separation?
questions.answer: If each additional nucleon occupies roughly the same volume, total nuclear volume is proportional to \(A\). Since volume scales as \(R^3\), this gives \(R\propto A^{1/3}\), matching the empirical radius law.

questions.prompt: A nuclide has \(N/Z=1.50\) and \(A=100\). Find \(Z\) and \(N\).
Explain why the atomic mass number \(A\) is close to, but not exactly equal to, the atomic mass in atomic mass units.
questions.answer: \(A\) counts nucleons, and each nucleon has mass close to \(1\,\mathrm u\). The actual atomic mass differs because proton and neutron masses are not exactly \(1\,\mathrm u\), electrons contribute slightly, and binding energy reduces the total mass.

questions.prompt: Show that doubling the nuclear radius increases the approximate nucleon number by a factor of \(8\).
questions.answer:
From \(R=R_0A^{1/3}\),
\[
A=\left( rac{R}{R_0}ight)^3
\]
If \(R\) doubles, \(A\) changes by \(2^3=8\).

questions.prompt: A scattering experiment estimates a nuclear radius. Explain why high-energy probes are needed to resolve nuclear size.
questions.answer: To resolve a length scale \(R\), the probe wavelength must be comparable to or smaller than \(R\). De Broglie wavelength satisfies \(\lambda=h/p\), so femtometre resolution requires large momentum and therefore high-energy particles.

questions.prompt: Prove that if nuclear density is constant and nuclear mass is proportional to \(A\), then \(R\propto A^{1/3}\).
questions.answer:
Constant density means
\[
ho= rac{M}{V}\approx rac{Au}{(4/3)\pi R^3}=	ext{constant}
\]
Thus
\[
R^3\propto A
\]
and therefore
\[
R\propto A^{1/3}
\]
This is the inverse argument behind the radius law.
